title: Agent identity and attribution of agent actions
status_rationale: Praxis (praxis@12bf9951, v3.25.0) records a stable actor identity (agent, human, automation) with provider, model and runtime, plus execution identity, on work events and canonical artifacts in repositories that use it (docs/agent-provenance.md in this repository). That covers engineering provenance only. Runtime agent identity for a product (AIN-013, SOC2-017, GOV-AUTH-006) is designed but not built, and Praxis attribution has not been independently verified.
target_answer: Every agent, in engineering and in the product, has a unique non-shared identity distinct from human users. Each action records agent identity, model and prompt version, tool, initiating human or principal, delegation chain and effective permission (AIN-013). Agent credentials are short-lived and bound to the run. Sub-agent delegation carries attribution and cannot amplify authority (AIN-010). Records are append-only and tamper-evident, retained as audit evidence.
current_practice: Engineering: Praxis provenance attributes work events and canonical artifact contributions to agent identities, executions and runs in repositories that use it. Product: none, as no production system exists.
intended_practice: Extend the Praxis actor model to runtime agents through the Unbound evidence envelope (SOC2-002) and AIN-013 fields.
provable: Praxis execution and event records in repositories that use Praxis show agent actor identity for engineering work. Not independently verified; not a production runtime control.
customer_statement: Echelon's repository operating system, Praxis, records which agent, provider, model and run produced engineering work in repositories that use it. This has not been independently verified and is not yet a runtime control for a production service; runtime agent identity and attribution are designed but not built.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon engineering owner for Praxis; Unbound platform owner for runtime)
residual_risks: Provenance identifies the agent and run but self-reported model identifiers may be 'unknown' (as seen in some Praxis records).

title: Least privilege and deterministic authorization for agents
status_rationale: Unbound defines authority tiers A0 to A5 and requires an authority registry (GOV-AUTH-001), no self-granted permissions (GOV-AUTH-003), deterministic, independently testable enforcement (GOV-AUTH-021), a single AuthorityMatrix that refuses unmapped commands (CNV-GOV-010) and a release-1 agent command set limited to reversible internal actions at A2 or below (CNV-AIO-001). Not implemented.
target_answer: Agent permissions are declared in the authority matrix per command class and actor type, approved by an authorized human, and enforced by deterministic server-side code. Unmapped commands are refused. Agents cannot grant or change their own permissions or approve their own outputs. In release 1 no agent can execute anything above A2. Repeated out-of-authority requests are rate-limited and reported to the agent owner, never escalated into a decision. Agent permissions are reviewed periodically and on change, and unused permissions are removed.
current_practice: Not established for any production service. Engineering agent permissions in repositories, CI and cloud accounts are not documented in any record located.
intended_practice: Implement CNV-GOV-010 and GOV-AUTH-001 through 004 and AUTH-T01, T04 negative tests.
customer_statement: Echelon's design limits AI agents to reversible internal actions, enforced by deterministic authorization outside the model, with no ability to grant themselves permissions. This is not yet implemented.
open_questions: What permissions do engineering agents hold today in source control, CI and any cloud account?

title: Reserved human authority for consequential actions; agents never hold human-authority operations or clear risk
status_rationale: Invariants exist in design: the Echelon AI-Native Enterprise Design Framework (Echelon-AI-Native-Enterprise-Design-Framework@763ff8c:AGENTS.md rule 5; src/Echelon.Enterprise/Model.fs NoAiClearance) requires that human authority is preserved, AI never clears under NoAiClearance and agents never hold human-authority operations, and this is tested in that framework's property tests for its models. Unbound requires A4 reserved human authority for grant approval and other decisions (GOV-AUTH tiers), approval bound to an exact proposal and evidence snapshot (GOV-AUTH-009, AIN-022), independent reconciliation (GOV-AUTH-014), segregation of duties enforced by the engine (CNV-GOV-003), A4 approval by a human who did not prepare the item (RR-AIN-003-r1) and board-delegated deterministic policy with quarterly reporting (CNV-GOV-008). Live payments are A5 currently (GOV-AUTH-019). None is implemented in a product.
target_answer: AI agents may observe, prepare and recommend. They never approve grants, release payments, change bank or payee details, instruct trades, clear sanctions, fraud or eligibility concerns, or exercise any reserved authority. Only an authorized human, or a deterministic rule that a sponsor board has delegated in writing with limits and expiry, can clear or decide. Approval binds to a hash of the exact proposal and evidence; any material change invalidates it. The approver must be someone other than the preparer, and the agent that initiated a transaction cannot attest to its reconciliation. Anti-rubber-stamp measures include risk-stratified sampling of approved items, approval-time metrics and required review of the deterministic findings section.
current_practice: Design invariants and requirements only. No product exists.
intended_practice: Implement the authority matrix with A4 and A5 tiers and the approval binding before any agent feature ships.
provable: The EDF invariant tests demonstrate the rule inside a design framework, not in a production system. Nothing operational.
customer_statement: In Echelon's design, AI agents can never approve, release funds, change payees, clear sanctions or fraud alerts, or hold any human-authority operation; only authorized humans or sponsor-delegated deterministic rules can decide. This is enforced in Echelon's design framework tests but not yet in a production system.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: sponsor board for delegation; Unbound product owner for enforcement)
residual_risks: Automation bias: a human may approve AI-prepared items without real review.
Delegated deterministic rules can encode errors that clear many items at once.

challenge.customer_intent: Customers and regulators want a responsible human accountable for every consequential decision.
challenge.adverse_outcome: An AI or automated process approves a prohibited grant, pays a sanctioned party or clears a real alert.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Requiring a human click on every item is weak when volume is high: approvers rubber-stamp, and accountability becomes nominal.
challenge.legally_required: Sponsor boards hold legal control of DAF assets; IRC 4966 and 4967 and OFAC obligations sit with the sponsor. No law requires a human click per item, but fiduciary duty cannot be delegated to software.
challenge.contractually_required: Sponsor agreements typically reserve grant approval to the sponsor.
challenge.architectural_elimination: AI clearance is removed structurally: no command exists through which an agent can clear or approve. Board-delegated deterministic rules handle routine, fully-specified cases with limits and expiry.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: The engine enforces segregation of duties and approval binding on every action.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Quarterly board report of auto-approved, held and declined items (CNV-GOV-008); sampling results.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Deterministic, board-delegated rules for routine items plus focused human judgment on exceptions, instead of human approval of every item.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Delegation records, rule versions, sampling outcomes and denial logs are auditable.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If rule inputs are incomplete or stale, deterministic clearance can be wrong at scale; the delegation must expire and be re-reviewed.
challenge.alternative_risks: Systematic errors in a delegated rule affect many items before detection.
supporting_arguments: Human attention goes to items that need judgment.
Rules are testable and reproducible, humans are not.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain; some sponsors and auditors expect a human approval per grant regardless of rule quality.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Board delegation may be misunderstood as AI approval by observers.
Requires sponsor governance maturity to delegate properly.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

history.change: BL-021: set institutional_acceptance to unknown (prior 'uncertain' was unsourced agent judgment, kept in supporting_arguments) and added an unvalidated-acceptance note to opposing_arguments (OBJ-VRM-019, OBJ-SKEPTIC-014).

title: Interruptibility, emergency stop and safe degradation
status_rationale: SOC2-017 requires agents to be interruptible; GOV-AUTH-024 requires emergency stop, agent suspension, safe mode and human takeover with evidence and recovery approval; AIN-018 requires pause and cancel with explicit in-flight semantics; CNV-AIO-001 requires deterministic paths to continue when AI is unavailable; AUTH-T07 tests emergency stop. Not implemented.
target_answer: Authorized humans can suspend a single agent, an agent class or all agents immediately. Queued autonomous actions are safely suspended, in-flight steps settle to an explicit state, and nothing irreversible proceeds after the stop. Deterministic processes continue without AI. Resumption requires recorded approval and revalidation of authority and evidence (AIN-017, AIN-020). Emergency stop is tested on a schedule and evidence of each test is kept.
customer_statement: Echelon's design provides an emergency stop for AI agents with safe suspension of queued actions and continued operation of deterministic processes. Not yet implemented or tested.

title: Decision accountability records and explainability
status_rationale: UNB-AI-STD-002 and RR-UNB-AI-STD-002-r1 require capture of evidence, uncertainty, model and prompt version, policy version and human sign-off; AIN-005 separates fact, inference, recommendation and decision; AIN-026 allows challenge of agent facts; GOV-AUTH-022 and GOV-AUTH-017 require replayable decisions and reproducible Folio decision packages. Not implemented.
target_answer: Every consequential decision has a record naming the accountable human or delegated rule, the exact evidence snapshot, what AI contributed and in which model and prompt version, the policy version applied and the outcome. Facts, inferences, recommendations and decisions are labeled distinctly. Affected parties can challenge an AI-contributed fact and get independent human review with preserved provenance. Decision packages can be replayed and rendered for auditors and examiners.
intended_practice: Implement the evidence envelope (SOC2-002) and Folio decision packages.
customer_statement: Echelon's design records, for every consequential decision, who decided, what evidence they saw, what AI contributed and which policy applied, and lets affected parties challenge AI-contributed facts. Not yet implemented.

title: Reliability of AI-generated or AI-processed control and audit evidence
status_rationale: SOC2-004 requires evidence as a byproduct of operations, SOC2-008 forbids marking controls operating without observed evidence, SOC2-031 separates production from test evidence, GOV-AUTH-011 bars agent-generated claims from becoming binding without review, AIN-033 treats missing agent traces as deficiencies, and A5 prohibits falsifying evidence or disabling logs (AUTH-T08). RR-REQ-X-073-r2 limits AI to extracting vendor report metadata for human confirmation. Continuous control monitoring architecture is specified, not implemented.
target_answer: Control evidence is produced by deterministic systems as a byproduct of operation, signed and hash-chained, never authored by AI. AI may summarize or extract, but summaries are labeled, link to the underlying records and are never accepted as evidence on their own. Agents have no write or delete access to evidence or logs. Test and synthetic evidence is labeled and stored apart from production evidence. When an AI summary is found wrong, the summary is withdrawn, dependent assertions are flagged and the correction is recorded.
current_practice: Not established. In this due diligence repository, AI agents draft research records under schema validation and honesty checks (tools/build.fsx flags aspirational statements presented as current), but human review status of those records is not recorded.
intended_practice: Implement the evidence envelope and continuous control monitoring with AI restricted to labeled summaries.
provable: The build tool in this repository rejects answer units that state current facts without an implemented status; that is a first-party check on AI-drafted content, not evidence of control operation.
customer_statement: Echelon's design requires control evidence to be generated by deterministic systems and protected from alteration by AI agents; AI summaries are labeled and never accepted as evidence on their own. Not yet implemented.

challenge.customer_intent: Auditors and customers need evidence they can trust; AI involvement raises fabrication and error concerns.
challenge.adverse_outcome: AI-produced evidence or summaries misstate control operation and an auditor or customer relies on them.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Manually assembled evidence packages before an audit are also error-prone and selective; they are not inherently more reliable than machine-produced records.
challenge.legally_required: Not legally specified; auditing standards require the auditor to evaluate reliability of information produced by the entity.
challenge.contractually_required: Audit clauses assume evidence is complete and accurate.
challenge.historical_convention: Screenshots and spreadsheets assembled by staff.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Evidence authorship by AI is removed: agents have no write path to evidence stores; evidence emerges from deterministic operations.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Hash chains and missing-heartbeat exceptions (SOC2-027) on every evidence stream.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Evidence by construction from deterministic systems, with AI limited to labeled navigation and summary.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Auditor can verify hash chains and sample underlying records.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If evidence generators themselves are written by AI agents without adequate review, generator correctness becomes the question.
challenge.alternative_risks: Evidence generators are code and can be wrong; auditors will test information produced by the entity.
supporting_arguments: Completeness and failures are visible, not only successes (SOC2-005).

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely among auditors familiar with system-generated evidence; IPE testing will still be required.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Generator code may be AI-written, which shifts trust to the generator's review.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Reliability of AI-completed questionnaires and customer-facing assertions
status_rationale: This knowledge base is drafted by AI research agents. Its build tool (tools/build.fsx) is an internal research integrity check on this repository: it compares two metadata fields set by the same author (status and customer_statement_kind), applies a heuristic wording lint, fails on em dashes and dangling references, and flags independent assurance claims. It does not read evidence and cannot tell whether a status is true, so it is not a customer safeguard. Each record carries a history entry naming the creating agent role. Since 2026-11-25 the operating contract requires named human approval before any release and the build fails on an approval without a named human, but no answer unit has been approved and none has been released to a customer.
target_answer: Echelon tells customers when questionnaire answers are AI-drafted. Every answer is generated from a canonical answer unit with a controlled status, a customer statement that internal checks compare against that status (an integrity aid, not assurance), cited evidence and sources, and a named human signatory who reviews and accepts accountability before release. Answers are reproducible: the same answer unit yields the same response across questionnaires, and changes are versioned.
current_practice: Canonical answer units with honesty checks exist in this repository; human review and signatory process do not.
intended_practice: Define a release step requiring a named human signatory per questionnaire response and record it.
provable: Repository contents and build tool rules show the honesty checks; there is no record of human review.
customer_statement: Echelon's questionnaire answers are drafted with AI from an internal answer library. The library has internal consistency checks used for research integrity; they do not verify that an answer is true and are not a customer safeguard. No answer has yet been approved by a named human reviewer, and Echelon will release no answer until a named human has reviewed it and accepts accountability for it.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon managing member as signatory)
residual_risks: Build checks test consistency between status and statement, not whether the status itself is true.
The build check never reads evidence and compares fields set by the same author; it can pass a wrong status consistently.
AI tools used to draft answers may process customer questionnaire text; which tools and under which provider terms is not yet recorded (OBJ-PRIVACY-011).

challenge.customer_intent: Customers rely on questionnaire answers as representations; they want them accurate and attributable to an accountable person.
challenge.adverse_outcome: An AI-drafted answer claims a control that does not exist, and the customer relies on it.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Human-completed questionnaires are frequently inaccurate, copied from old answers and inconsistent across customers.
challenge.legally_required: Misrepresentation liability applies regardless of authorship.
challenge.contractually_required: Contracts often incorporate questionnaire answers as representations.
challenge.historical_convention: Security team fills spreadsheets manually per request.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Not eliminated. The build tool flags inconsistency between status and statement kind and some unhedged wording; it is an internal research integrity check, not a customer safeguard, and only named human review can establish that a statement is true.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Schema, status-to-kind and wording heuristics on every build; human approval gate for release (no approvals yet).
challenge.continuous_evidence: Every answer traces to an answer unit with status, evidence and history.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Governed answer library with machine-checked honesty plus human signatory, instead of free-form human answers.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Customers can request the answer unit, evidence references and history.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If statuses are set wrongly at source, checks propagate the error consistently.
challenge.alternative_cost: low per questionnaire after library investment
challenge.alternative_risks: Consistency can spread one wrong status to many customers.
supporting_arguments: Honesty rule is enforced, not hoped for.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely if disclosed and signed by an accountable person; unlikely if AI drafting is concealed.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Some customers distrust AI-drafted answers on principle.
Status accuracy still depends on human verification.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Governance of AI agents in engineering and operations: change approval, segregation and access
status_rationale: Echelon builds software largely with AI coding agents. Unbound requires two approvers, neither the author, on control-relevant modules (CNV-PLT-010), deterministic release gate rules for segregation (CNV-GOV-003), change approval and emergency change evidence (SOC2-011), and no agent self-approval (GOV-AUTH-003). Whether Echelon repositories currently require human approval before merge, and what production or cloud access agents have, is not documented in any record located. Praxis records agent provenance and has a work protocol with completion evidence.
target_answer: AI coding and operations agents can propose changes but cannot merge to protected branches, release, deploy or change production configuration without approval by an authorized human who did not prompt the change; control-relevant modules need two such approvers (CNV-PLT-010). An agent or model session cannot both author and approve. Agents get no standing production access and no break-glass access; production operations by agents are limited to read-only diagnostics scoped and approved per CNV-ARC-002, with any write requiring per-case human approval. A named human is accountable for every merged change regardless of author.
intended_practice: Configure branch protection and CI approval rules across Echelon repositories and document them; apply CNV-ARC-002 operator access rules to agents.
provable: Praxis provenance can show which agent produced a change. Nothing proves approval controls.
customer_statement: Echelon uses AI coding agents to develop its software. It intends that agents never merge, release or operate production without approval by an accountable human who did not prompt the change. Those controls are not yet documented or evidenced.
residual_risks: With a very small team, independent human approval may be the same few people for every change, limiting real segregation.
open_questions: Are branch protection and required human reviews enabled on Echelon repositories today?
How many humans are available to act as independent approvers?
